faqs.q: Where do people give birth in Hialeah?
faqs.a: Most Hialeah births happen at Palmetto General Hospital in the heart of the city, which runs the Maternity Child Care Center with in-house neonatal care and labor suites. Families who want a bigger hospital program go to the Orlando Health Bayfront Hospital Center for Women and Babies a few minutes west, and out-of-hospital families use Magnolia Birth House in North Miami Beach or a licensed home-birth midwife.

faqs.q: Does Palmetto General Hospital allow doulas?
faqs.a: Yes. Doulas are welcome as support persons at Palmetto General - the maternity program is built around family-centered care, including skin-to-skin time immediately after delivery. Hospital policies on exactly how many support persons you can bring can change, so confirm the current rule at your hospital tour or with your OB's office before your due date.

faqs.q: What does a birth doula cost in Hialeah?
faqs.a: Expect roughly $900 to $2,400 for a full birth package, with postpartum-only packages priced lower and cesarean-specific coaching sometimes billed separately. Miami metro pricing has climbed in the last few years; every practice on this page publishes or confirms its own rate, so book a consultation before comparing. Florida Medicaid has covered doula services for eligible families since 2023, which changes the math entirely for enrolled families.

faqs.q: Are there midwife-attended options near Hialeah?
faqs.a: Yes, though the community is smaller than Miami's. Licensed midwives practice out of Hialeah itself and the adjacent Miami corridor, and certified nurse-midwives in the area work with Palmetto General Hospital for midwife-led prenatal care with a nearby hospital backup. For a fully midwife-attended, non-hospital birth, Magnolia Birth House in North Miami Beach is the closest dedicated center.

faqs.q: Do doulas here work with Spanish-speaking families?
faqs.a: Increasingly, yes - Hialeah is one of the most Spanish-speaking cities in America, and practices that serve the neighborhood treat bilingual capacity as baseline, not a premium. Inara Arauz and the Hialeah-based practices on this page all support families in both languages; ask directly if your family plans to use Spanish with the doula during labor.
